message.content:
This is a textile fabric coated with polyurethane, where the plastic coating is visible and makes up most of the weight. The question is whether it belongs in Chapter 59 or Chapter 39.

Heading 5903 covers textile fabrics coated with plastics. Note 2(a)(2) to Chapter 59 excludes products where the plastic is visible and the fabric serves only as backing, but that is for heading 3921 consideration. Heading 3921 covers plastic sheets, plates, and strip, including cellular plastic combined with textile. Chapter 39 Note 2 and Chapter 59 Note 2 deal with this overlap.

Chapter 59 Note 2(a)(1) covers impregnated, coated, or covered textile fabrics weighing not more than 1,500 g/m² (these fall in 5903 regardless of the plastic content). The weight here is 470 g/m², so it falls under 5903. Cellular plastics are handled in 5903 as well, since Note 2(b)(5) of Chapter 59 excludes plates and sheets of cellular plastics combined with textile fabric, where the textile is merely for reinforcement. Here the fabric is a real woven fabric that is dyed and napped, so it is not merely reinforcement. This points to 5903.

Within 5903, polyurethane coating falls under 5903.20 (with polyurethane). The statistical suffix for 5903.20.25 is "Other" for fabrics, and the 5903.20.2500 line covers coated fabrics with a plastic content over 70% by weight... Here the plastic is 63.4%. The subheadings for 5903.20 are: 5903.20.10 (pile fabrics), 5903.20.20 (laminated with a layer of fabric, 70% or more plastic by weight?), and 5903.20.25 (other). With 63.4% plastic and no lamination, the best fit is 5903.20.2500.
